recipes.name: Lasagna Alfredo
ingredients_raw: 3 cooked, boneless chicken breast halves, diced
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add lasagna noodles and cook until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes; drain.

Place frozen spinach and 1/2 cup water in a 2-quart nonstick saucepan; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-high, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally, until spinach is tender, 6 to 7 minutes. Drain and squeeze out any excess water.
Stir together chicken and 1 jar Alfredo sauce in a medium bowl until well combined.
Mix together ricotta and spinach in a second medium bowl until well combined.

Arrange a single layer of lasagna noodles in a 9x13-inch baking dish, edges overlapping. Pour chicken-Alfredo mixture over noodles and spread evenly. Sprinkle with 1 cup mozzarella. Cover with another layer of noodles. Spread spinach mixture evenly over noodles. Pour 1/2 of the remaining jar of Alfredo sauce over spinach mixture and spread evenly. Sprinkle with 1 cup mozzarella. Lay on a final noodle layer and top with remaining 1/2 jar Alfredo sauce and 2 cups mozzarella. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is brown and bubbly, 50 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Lasagna Alfredo
raw_recipe.description: This chicken Alfredo lasagna features layers of noodles, ricotta, spinach, creamy white sauce, and mozzarella cheese for a family-favorite dinner.

review.reviewBody: I added extra chicken to this recipe. Also, did not follow the recommended layering technique. I made this lasagna the way I make my regular lasagna: 1) mixed ALL of the alfredo sauce with the chicken; 2) put a little sauce on bottom of pan so it won't stick; 3)layer of noodles; 4) layer of chicken/sauce mixture; 5)layer of mozzarella; 6) layer of spinach. Repeat last three layers two more times. Cover and bake 50-60 minutes, than uncover, add mozzarella cheese on top and bake until chees is golden.

Served this at a dinner party and got rave reviews! I doubled the recipe, used the lasagna noodles you don't have to cook, Classico Roasted Garlic Alfredo sauce and added 1 bunch of chopped spring onions to the sauce. I also spread about a cup of the sauce on the bottom of the pan before adding the noodles so they didn't stick, then mixed the chicken in with the rest of the sauce and put about another cup of it on top of the last layer of noodles before adding the cheese.

Really tasty but VERY rich. I made a smaller portion in an 8x8 Pyrex using: 15oz ricotta, 10oz spinach (sautéed in a little olive oil), 1c mozzarella, 1/3c fresh grated Parmesan and s&p all mixed together for the filling. I sautéed 2 chicken breast in olive oil, then cooled and sliced them and also made my own Alfredo sauce (2 tablespoon butter, 2 tbslp flour to make a roux, then added 1c half & half and 1c milk. Once warmed through, added 8oz fresh grated Parmesan, salt & pepper) spooned enough sauce into the baking dish to cover the bottom, added a layer of noodles, half the ricotta/spinach mixture, then covered with sauce. Added another layer of noodles, remaining spinach mixture, the chicken slices, and covered the chicken with sauce. Finally, 1 last layer of noodles, sauce, and then covered with 1c of mozzarella. Placed on a cookie sheet and baked, uncovered, for 50 minutes. My husband, who doesn't care for spinach, had 2 helpings as did our son, who went on to ask what he'd have to do in order to get me to make this on a regular basis. It was absolutely delicious, but I don't even want to think of the fat and calories! Definitely a guilty pleasure and something I'd probably only make occasionally.

So I really quite enjoyed this recipe and the family was really impressed, we got a new oven and wanted to try a new recipe so we landed on this one and we weren't disappointed. The only changes I made to the recipe which I do think were welcoming touches was that I added 1/2 cup of diced green onion to the spinach, I added one cup of Bella Rosa parmesan(Or any parmesan you want really should work), and then we also added some Cajun seasoning to the chicken when we cooked it separately. The flavor was really good with this recipe and the chicken was so tender and juicy we will definitely be making this again.

Best lasagne ever. I found the recipe in the Fall 2017 issue of the Allrecipes magazine and the printed version only called for half the mozarella (2 cups) and ricotta (1 pint) cheeses. I used a 9x13 pan and only ended up needing 9 lasagne noodles. I grilled the chicken breasts, mixed all of the alfredo sauce with the chicken and spread a thin layer of sauce on the bottom of the pan to prevent sticking as another reviewer suggested. I also added about a quarter cup of diced sweet onion to the spinach/garlic/ricotta mixture. I did one layer of noodles (3), spread 1/3 of the ricotta mixture, then 1/3 of of the chicken/alfredo mixture, then 1/3 of the mozarella with a little bit of shredded parmesan. For a little extra flavor, I spread about a tablespoon of fresh chopped oregano and then layered fresh basil leaves from my garden, about one leaf per piece. The herbs added a much richer flavor and I dont think the dish would've been nearly as good without them. I then did another layer of noodles (3), 1/3 of the ricotta mixture, 1/3 of the chicken/alfredo mixture, 1/3 of the mozarella & parmesan. I repeated with 3 more noodles and the remainders of the 2 mixtures and cheese. I topped with some fresh grated parmesan and baked for about an hour at 350. For a side, I buttered and toasted slices of Italian bread, then scraped each side with a fresh clove of garlic. Absolutely delicious! I will definitely make this dish again!

With a majority of the ingredients being fresh, why would use bottled alfredo sauce? (or frozen spinach for that matter) Wilt down your own spinach and add, and make your own fresh alfredo, it couldn't be easier. Equal parts butter, parmesean, and heavy cream. Melt the butter, stir together with the other ingredients. Add seasonings if you like. I'm a big fan of basil and oregano and fresh diced garlic. Would rate it five stars if prepared this way.

It clearly benefitted from my enhancements as follows: 
1. I cubed 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts, sauteed them in avocado oil until just cooked with tarragon, herbes de provence, 2 minced garlic cloves, lemon pepper, couple of other handy spices incl. S&P
2. I lightly fried a half bunch of green onions with about 5 small portabello mushrooms which I added on top of the spinach layer
3. Added an extra cup of Moz for the top
4. I used the Classico roasted garlic alfredo sauce as another reviewer suggested

Next time will add something to make the sauce a bit runnier. Ours was a bit too thick.

Delicious recipe! After I diced the chicken, I added salt and pepper and then sauteed in a pan with some onion. Like others did, I added the chicken in with Classico Garlic Alfredo sauce. I also used a mixture of mozzarella and parmesan in all layers of cheese. On the top I put some sauce on the last noodle layer before the cheese and then seasoned with salt and pepper on the very top. My husband and I loved it !! Will definitely be making this again!

I made 1/2 the recipe in an 8x8 pan but used all the spinach recipe called for. Added a little Italian seasoning and parsley to the ricotta spinach mix. Also used no cook noodles. It was very flavorful and delicious, I used the Classico garlic Alfredo sauce. Plenty for 2 dinners for two of us. I also added a little Parmesan in the cheese layers

Enjoyed this very much. Used slightly less mozzarella cheese, but other ingredients were the stated amounts. I did use Barilla no-boil lasagna noodles, which are wonderful. You do need to be sure the noodles are completely covered with sauce so they don't dry out during baking. I also sauteed a shallot and some garlic with the chicken for added flavor, and added some of the usual herbs and spices we like. I did add 2 eggs to the spinach/ricotta mixture, as I normally do that anyway. Baked the first 25 min covered with foil to keep moist, then uncovered for the rest of the time. Everyone loved it, and it makes a ton,so we even had leftovers. Excellent recipe.

I put together day before & used no boil noodles. Refrigerated overnight & baked next day. It was really good. Plan to make again in few days. This cut down baking time to about 50 min. I also used a Lawry Salt rub on chicken breasts. Going to try it with shrimp instead of chicken.
We added broccoli and onion and gr pepper to it ! No spinach

Huge hit at Christmas Eve dinner! Prepped it night before with fresh spinach and using Ina's homemade alfredo sauce. Did add onions as suggested. And like many reviews before recipes makes a lot! Can't wait to do it again.

I liked it, next time I will make a few changes to better suit my personal tastes (additional seasonings, less ricotta, more alfredo, more chicken, more cheese, maybe some cheddar?), but this makes for a great recipe to base your own spin off of!

Since I’m allergic to tomatoes and black pepper, this was a great dish. I used 2lbs of Mozzarella and doubled up on chicken. I boiled me chicken and shredded it. Then added everything as directed. Definitely a great recipe!
I used canned chicken browned in the skillet with butter (all I had) and thawed but didn’t pre cook the spinach. Other than that, I followed the recipe. Looks delicious! It’s what’s for dinner.
Easy to follow recipe. Tasted good. Think I will add more meat next time and more Alfredo sauce between layers

My Husband requested chicken alfredo lasagna for Valentine's Day. It was a hit with our family of four. My Husband went back for seconds, that made me so happy! It'll definitely be something I make more of in the future. I love to cook but this was my first time making lasagna. I tweaked this recipe with some leftover ingredients and it came out good also. I think this is a great recipe to follow and then add your own twist to it. Highly recommended!
